text:
Claude Giroux is 38, has played 1,000 games for Philadelphia and more than 300 for Ottawa, and came into this season with over 1,165 career points. He is still a top-nine center who matters. Ten points in 17 games is right on last season's pace (49 points in 82), and nothing in his shooting is lucky or unlucky: three goals on almost exactly three goals' worth of chances.

The interesting split is in how Ottawa plays with him on. The Senators are slightly behind on shot attempts at 5v5 (48.7%) but well ahead on chance quality (55.4% of the expected goals), which says his group gives up volume and takes the good looks. His teammates have scored about three goals fewer than those chances deserve, so a few more assists should come. Evolving-Hockey rated him a strong defensive forward last season (89th percentile at suppressing chances), worth 2.1 wins overall, 47th among forwards. His ice time over the last ten games is down about a minute, which is the thing to watch for a player his age. Our projection lands near 49 points again. Steady, which at 38 is its own kind of remarkable.
headline: Giroux at 38: still steady, still useful
